mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Elevated convection developing across southwest North Dakota may continue to intensify and pose a severe threat over the next few hours, though confidence in exact evolution is uncertain

details.label: Summary
details.text: Elevated convection developing across southwest North Dakota may continue to intensify and pose a severe threat over the next few hours, though confidence in exact evolution is uncertain

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convection has been gradually intensifying to the west of Bismarck, ND over the past 45 minutes, and a few additional updrafts are noted to the southwest of this cell per GOES IR imagery. This activity appears to be driven by weak ascent within a diffuse low-level baroclinic zone draped from southwest ND southeastward into SD based on recent upper-air analyses. Although this activity is somewhat displaced to the north of the axis of greater buoyancy (and is upstream of the cold pool associated with a leading supercell in SD), the 00 UTC BIS RAOB and recent forecast soundings suggest buoyancy should be adequate for sustained deep convection downstream into south-central ND. Additionally, strong deep-layer shear remains in place across the region and can support intense supercell development (as evident by the aforementioned supercell in SD, which matured in a similar kinematic environment). Despite the favorable convective environment, it remains unclear whether this emerging cell will remain isolated or if additional convection will emerge within this zone and foster upscale growth along the baroclinic zone into SD later tonight. Convective trends will continue to be monitored, and watch issuance may be needed as dictated by storm evolution and intensity

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The threat for very large hail and severe winds will continue as a robust supercell migrates southeast across western South Dakota

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for very large hail and severe winds will continue as a robust supercell migrates southeast across western South Dakota

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Over the past hour, a lone, but intense, supercell has exhibited persistent three-body scatter spikes consistent with very large hail, and has also produced wind gusts of at least 61 mph per recent reports. More recently, the reflectivity core has diminished slightly, and the storm motion has shifted from due south to southeasterly, suggesting a slight weakening of the storm's internal pressure perturbations and overall intensity. However, this cell will continue to reside within an environment very favorable for intense convection (MLCAPE near 4000 J/kg and nearly 50 knots of effective bulk shear as sampled by the 00 UTC UNR and ABR soundings), so some degree of re-intensification appears possible. Additionally, new updraft development is noted on the western flank of the cell, which may also intensify and pose a threat for very large (2 inch) hail and severe gusts. Given the elongated/straight nature of regional wind profiles, the emergence of this new cell hints that cell interactions and cold pool amalgamation may increase over the next couple of hours as the new cell begins to split. This may result in a very gradual transition from a supercellular to a clustered/linear storm mode with an attendant increase in severe wind potential as storms move further south/southeast. A few recent high-res solutions hint at this transition, but confidence in this scenario is somewhat limited at this point due to the isolated nature of the convection
